content.en: The **International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)** was established in 1977 as a result of the 1974 World Food Conference. It functions as both a specialized UN agency and an international financial institution. Its primary focus is to empower rural poor people in developing countries to increase their food production, improve their nutrition, and raise their incomes.

content.en: India is a founding member of IFAD and has been a significant recipient of its loans and grants to support agricultural transformation and rural livelihoods.

content.en: Do not confuse IFAD with the FAO; while they collaborate, IFAD is specifically a financial institution providing loans and grants.

content.en: Focus on how IFAD aligns with India's goal of doubling farmers' income and sustainable agriculture.
